Simplify under the square root, then compute roots. For example, if f(x) = x² – 5x + 6, plug into the formula to find x = 2 or 3. Double-check by substituting back!

Stationary points occur where f'(x) = 0 (critical points). First, differentiate y = f(x) to get f'(x). Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. Then plug these x-values back into f(x) to find corresponding y-coordinates. For example, if f(x) = x³ – 3x² + 2, find f'(x) = 3x² – 6x, set to zero: x(3x – 6) = 0 → x = 0 or 2. Check y-values at these points.
